To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the folic acid receptor is over-expressed in several types of human cancers and that this receptor can be used for targeted therapy.
the folate receptor is expressed on the surface of a number of human tumor cells, including those from the ovary, breast, and lung.
the folic acid receptor is differentially expressed between normal and tumor cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of novel methods for the detection of cellular markers in normal and tumor tissues and their use in clinical studies.
the development of new methods to detect, quantify, and monitor tumor markers.
developing flow cytometric assays that can be used to measure the expression of folic acid transport receptors on tumor cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the use of folic acid in the treatment of folate deficiency anemia, the use of antifoldes for cancer therapy, and the use and development of flow cytometry are all interrelated and have had major impacts on medicine and science in the 20th century.

the folic acid receptor is a good target for cancer chemotherapy, and flow cytometric quantitation of the expression of this receptor is a useful tool for diagnosis and monitoring of treatment of patients with tumors that overexpress this receptor.

flow cytometry has provided an excellent means for quantifying the expression of important markers in cancer cells and has provided a means to monitor the effects of chemotherapy and radiation therapy on these markers.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have used flow cytometric detection and analysis of folic acid receptor in tumor cells to study the effect of antifolate therapy on cell proliferation, to study the role of folates in normal and tumor cells, and to use folates as a marker for detection of tumor cells in bone marrow and peripheral blood (9–13).

the folic acid receptor has a restricted expression in normal cells but has a high level of overexpression in a number of tumor types, and this differential expression can be used to target the tumor cells with folate-conjugated cytotoxins and imaging agents.
the folic acid receptor has been a useful marker for the differential diagnosis of malignant and nonmalignant tissues.
The main takeaway from our work is that

flow cytometric detection of the a-folate receptor can be used to identify and quantify tumor cells in a heterogeneous cell population and to determine the efficacy of folate receptor-targeted drug delivery systems in vitro (9,10).
the use of flow cytometry to study the expression of folate receptors in tumor cells is a powerful tool in the development of new therapies for treatment of cancer (9).
folic acid receptors are overexpressed in tumor cells and can be used as a target for tumor therapy.
